text:
maria g.: Quick question — should the console's role/scope selector also control per-route quotas, or should quotas live purely in the runtime/gateway? customer asked for a 'read-only' role that also gets a lower token quota on write routes. link: https://img.redwood/mock.png

alex k.: lean towards enforcement in the runtime/gateway. console should be the authoring surface, but enforcement at the edge avoids config drift and race conditions. if console only validates, callers can still hit the api if a rollout lag happens.

zoe: +1 on runtime enforcement but we need telemetry changes. runtime needs to surface role_id (or hashed role_id) in traces/metrics so we can tie usage to roles without leaking PII. current trace extraction drops user role metadata.

shawn: for rollout UX we can do a phased approach: 1) Console: preview effective permissions + "simulate as" to show expected behavior (no enforcement), 2) Canary: enforce for 5% of traffic, 3) Full enforcement. that reduces accidental lockouts.

liz (product): customers will expect a few things: preview/simulate, audit trail for who changed a role, and group sync (SSO) mapping. enterprise tenants will ask for retention SLAs on audit logs.

alex k.: API/implementation debate: two main options —
- Option A: enforce at runtime by adding scoped claims to tokens (e.g., `scopes` claim / role_id). runtime checks token claims per-route and applies quota. Requires token format bump and rollout.
- Option B: keep token format, have gateway consult policy service on each request (slower). Console writes policy service.
I prefer A for perf, B if we want zero token migration.

maria g.: migration concern: tokens are long-lived for some integrations. if we add scopes claim we need backward compatibility: runtime should accept old tokens (no scopes) but treat them as full-permission until migrated, and emit warnings in audit logs. That feels risky.

zoe: telemetry requirements if we go with A: add `permission_source` tag (token vs policy), emit `quota_enforced=true/false`, and expose per-role usage in console dashboards. Also add an alert when `quota_enforced` is false but usage is high (possible bypass).

shawn: implementation note: runtime can keep a lightweight in-memory policy cache keyed by tenant_id+role_digest; updates pushed over our existing pub/sub. policy size is tiny, so lookups are O(1). fallback to policy-service on cache miss.

deploy-bot: deploy: role-service v2 rolled out to canary at 2025-05-02T14:23Z :rocket:

liz (product): next steps — draft RFC outlining API change (token claim vs policy lookup), UX mocks for simulate-as & quota preview, and a migration plan + audit retention ask. I'll sync with legal on retention. Who wants to co-author the RFC?

alex k.: I can take the API section and runtime impact notes.

zoe: I'll write telemetry & metrics spec.

maria g.: I'll do the UX mockups for the simulate view and effective quota preview.

shawn: happy to write rollout steps and the runtime caching design.

liz (product): awesome, I'll assemble into a single RFC doc and share a draft next week. :thumbsup:
